p: thee with mirth: Solomon makes this discourse with himself, as though he would try whether there was contentment in ease and pleasures.
wisdom: Even though I gave myself to pleasures, yet I thought to keep wisdom and the fear of God in my heart, and govern my affairs by the same.
house: Meaning, of the servants or slaves which he had bought, so the children born in their servitude, were the masters.
delights of the sons of men: That is, whatever men take pleasure in.
as musical instruments: Or, the most beautiful of the women that were taken in war, as in Jud 5:30.
remained with me: For all this God did not take his gift of wisdom from me.
portion of all my labour: This was the fruit of all my labour, a certain pleasure mixed with care, which he calls vanity in the next verse.
wisdom: I thought to myself whether it was better to follow wisdom, or my own affections and pleasures, which he calls madness.
eyes are in his head: Meaning, in this world.
event happeneth to them all: For both die and are forgotten as in Ec 2:16 or they both alike have prosperity or adversity.
for ever: Meaning, in this world.
how dieth the wise man: He wonders that men forget a wise man, being dead, as soon as they do a fool.
to despair of all the labour: That I might seek the true happiness which is in God.

leave it for his portion: Among other griefs that was not the least, to leave that which he had gotten by great travail, to one who had taken no pain therefore and whom he know not whether he were a wise man or a fool.
make his soul enjoy good in: When man has all laboured, he can get no more than food and refreshing, yet he confesses also that this comes from God's blessing, as in Ec 3:13.
